neighbours.label: loss-of-sharpness terms in photography and optics (blur, blurry, out of focus, autofocus, ghosting, low pass filter); not 'focus' or 'ghost' in non-optical senses. The - pole is the tonal side of image quality (contrast, dynamic range)
fire: At slow shutter speeds the moving cars show obvious motion blur.
The background of the portrait is pleasantly blurred by the wide aperture.
Half of my holiday pictures turned out badly out of focus.
The new sensor has on-chip autofocus points across the whole frame.
A cheap filter on the front of the lens can cause ghosting around street lights.
The camera has no optical low pass filter, so fine detail looks crisper.
Shooting handheld at night left every frame soft and blurry.
The telescope image stays fuzzy until you refocus the eyepiece.
quiet: At rush hour the moving cars fill all four lanes of the bridge.
The background of the portrait is a plain grey studio wall.
Half of my holiday pictures were taken on the beach.
The new sensor has twenty-four megapixels and a faster processor.
A cheap strap on the camera can break without warning.
The camera has no built-in flash, so bring a small lamp.
The committee decided to focus on housing and transport this year.
The old house on the hill is said to have a ghost.
